expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: "Your fix is not enough — it's a heuristic that can fail in both directions." and a dedicated "Why your fix is insufficient" section.

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: "**Race condition** | Two workers check simultaneously before either writes → both charge" — the check-then-act window is named explicitly, and it is classed as a heuristic/warning rather than a device.

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: "// AFTER — control: required key\nfunction charge(customerId: CustomerId, amount: Money, idempotencyKey: IdempotencyKey)" plus "Make the parameter required".

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
expectations.evidence: "ALTER TABLE charges ADD CONSTRAINT uq_charge_idempotency UNIQUE (customer_id, idempotency_key);"

expectations.text: Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: "**Defect**: 340 customers charged twice / **Mistake**: The retry path called charge again... / **Hazard**: The charge operation has no idempotency enforcement"

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: "**Root hazard**: The system permits charging without an idempotency key, and nothing at the database or Stripe level rejects the duplicate." Queue redelivery is framed as "at-least-once, as designed".

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: "**Audit every queue consumer** — anywhere a retry can reach a charge, email, webhook, or external mutation needs an idempotency key" and an offer to "sweep your codebase for other non-idempotent retry paths" — the recommendation names concrete other side-effect classes, though the sweep itself is proposed rather than performed.

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: "**This is the second time** — that's the clearest signal you have a rung-0 fix masquerading as a control... The fact that it happened again means the previous fix also left the hazard open." — used to justify moving to the Control rung.

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: No person or team is blamed anywhere; causes are stated as "no idempotency key passed to Stripe", "no database constraint prevents duplicate charges", "Caller cannot forget" framed as a design property.
